text<jpn>: The peeling wallpaper is painfully bleak.
White curtains sway in the breeze.
Muddy footprints have been left across the wood-grain flooring.
The room is lit only by the light coming through the shattered windows.
The depth of the hole in the floor is impossible to see.
Spiderwebs cover every corner of the room.
The glass in the wooden-framed windows has been shattered.
The floor creaks with every step.
Wooden boards and sheets of metal have been propped up and left scattered about.
Dust hangs in the air. There is no doubt this place has been abandoned for a long time.
Tall lockers stand in long rows.
The blinds are drawn over the windows， leaving the room dim.
A solar-powered clock is still ticking away.
Several office desks have been left in rows.
Documents and ink stamps are scattered about.
Beyond the short hallway， there is a room containing little more than beds.
The black wallpaper gives the room a calm， subdued atmosphere.
A small chandelier hangs from the ceiling， and even the decorations on the doorknobs are ornate.
A dim path stretches ahead.
The linoleum floor seems to go on forever.
A gaudy chandelier hangs from the ceiling.
The cold concrete seems to swallow up the light.
It is dark and damp.
Only doors line the walls， and everything is silent.
The sound of drops falling can be heard from somewhere.
Black mold has grown between the pale blue tiles.
The sunlight coming through the window makes everything look almost dried out.
A filthy bathtub lies on the tiled floor.
Spiderwebs cover the place here and there.
A freestanding bathtub sits alone in the spacious room.
The shelves covered in spiderwebs are overflowing with things.
Things have been piled up carelessly， leaving barely any room to walk.
Tall shelves stand one after another， obstructing the view.
It is an eerie warehouse， the decaying wooden floorboards creaking underfoot.
The walls are made of cracked concrete.
The white walls and wood-grain floor evoke a vague sense of nostalgia.
An empty wok has been left sitting on a gas stove.
Something is rotting here and there.
It almost feels like the sound of something being stir-fried could start at any moment.
Several rugged racks stand scattered across the vast open space.
Torn packing materials have been thrown across the white floor.
Empty cardboard boxes are strewn everywhere.
Nothing remains but withered leaves.
Nothing but computers that would be of no use for surviving another day have been left behind.
Bookshelves cover an entire wall.
Colorful， unusual chairs stand in rows.
Silent computers sit lined up on the tables.
The chairs are filthy， but they must have been quite fine once.
A white staircase curves its way up to the second floor.
A staircase covered in red carpet leads up to the second floor.
At the center of the upper floor， a large portrait hangs above the staircase.
A chandelier hangs down from the open second floor.
There are no windows. The room is dimly lit only by the light coming through the door.
Shuttered shops stand one after another.
The shadows of utility poles fall heavily across the cracked asphalt.
The roadside trees have been knocked down.
The silent traffic lights look lonely.
Looking up， there is a pedestrian overpass stretching across the road.
Old houses stand one after another.
They have been overgrown with plants bursting out from everywhere.
Old houses and newly built apartments form a strange pattern.
The road is narrow. A one-way sign hangs there pointlessly.
The area is surrounded by abandoned fields.
The road slopes gently upward.
There are traces of what was once a small home garden.
An empty doghouse stands there forlornly.
Perhaps because of the lack of rain， the flowers have wilted.
It is a garden enclosed by concrete blocks.
It is surrounded by a high wall and covered with decorative gravel.
The ground is completely covered in gravel.
Perhaps some animal got inside; the place has been thoroughly ransacked.
Small lights hang from the ceiling beams.
Perhaps because of the wind， the support poles have become tilted.
Sleeping bags and empty cans of food have been left behind.
There are traces of soil being dug up and campfires being made.
Small white flowers bloom here and there.
A white trailer home sits in the distance.
Everything around is green.
A peaceful landscape stretches out before you.
Tall grass has grown thick across the entire area.
Fish can be seen swimming through the clear water.
Rounded stones can be seen scattered along the bottom.
The water source must be somewhere high up in the mountains.
The gentle current looks cool and refreshing.
Clear water and a calm breeze flow through the area.
The calls of wild birds can be heard.
Bits of trash and driftwood left behind by someone can be found here and there.
Everything is pure white as far as the eye can see.
The beach stretches out in a gentle arc.
The waves are calm.
The waves crash loudly， and the wind is strong.
The waves are surging violently against the shore.
Someone must have been here until recently; their belongings are soaked in seawater.
If you're not careful， your shoes will get wet.
Dark-colored seaweed can be seen washing ashore.
The spray kicked up by the waves is powerful along the water's edge.
A peaceful moment passes with the sea breeze.
Rows of tightly packed bookshelves stretch as far as the eye can see.
The book spines absorb all the light coming through the windows， leaving the room dim.
The bookshelves are missing books here and there.
The aisles are narrow.
Large books stand in long rows.
Machines whose purpose is impossible to tell stand in long rows.
Oil stains have seeped into the green mats.
Pieces of pitch-black rubber have been stuffed into metal drums.
The silence is eerie.
Footsteps echo throughout the spacious room.
The shutters have been left open， leaving the place empty and bare.
Everything that was brought inside has simply been left behind.
The warehouse in the back is filled with nothing but pitch darkness.
Cargo has been piled up.
There is only enough space for one car to park.
Abandoned cars are parked haphazardly.
Cars without their owners sit there silently.
Hardly any cars remain.
The asphalt is hot enough to scorch.
There is a payment machine at the exit.
Artifacts excavated from ancient ruins are displayed in rows.
Fossils of dinosaurs and prehistoric creatures hang from above.
Ancient books line the shelves behind glass.
The exhibits standing in the darkness are eerie.
The place is so vast that the light doesn't reach the back.
The overwhelming silence makes your legs tremble.
Perhaps from years without maintenance， parts of it look loose and unstable.
It sways in the wind， creaking softly.
Whatever happened here， discarded mascot costumes lie covered in dirt.
They are rusted solid and look as though they could never move again.
They probably never will.
It is white and spacious.
It shouldn't really be this large， but the stark room feels strangely vast.
White sheets have been neatly folded. Their meticulousness is strangely painful.
The whiteness of the walls is blinding. Even with only a little sunlight coming through the window， the white room seems to rise out of the darkness.
Even an after-school classroom was never this quiet.

The desks and chairs are neatly arranged.
It makes you wonder if the children might come back tomorrow morning.
Cream-colored curtains sway in the breeze.
For some reason， school classrooms always have a peculiar dimness to them.
A road without any lights stretches endlessly ahead.

A strong wind blows through.
Where did it come from， and where is it going?
Footsteps echo far into the distance.
The humidity is heavy enough to see.
Dust has settled over the tables as well.
The polished glasses sharply reflect the light coming through the windows.
Everything is so well maintained that it feels as though the day is about to begin.
Only a small amount of half-eaten food remains on the table.

What on earth is happening?
A strange sound can be heard， something like noise， but not quite.
A meaningless sequence of sounds suddenly begins to sound like a familiar melody.

It feels as though only footsteps are echoing.
But if so， is this place really spacious enough for the sound to echo?

You probably wouldn't be able to smell anything at all.
What would it feel like to have absolutely no smell whatsoever?
